newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia gold slides with limited hedging.
newsitem.headline: Australia gold slides with limited hedging.

text.p: Australian gold selling on Monday morning helped push prices further down but dealers see the strength of the Australian dollar acting as a barrier to hedging.
Dealers said about 200,000 ounces of gold would have been sold from Australia on Monday morning at the market's opening.
Australian dealers said that Australian producers were not hedging against gold at the moment.
Ben Suttie of Bell Commodities said "we're not seeing a lot (of hedging against gold)".
Active gold hedges had reasonably good cover and would generally not reinstate new short positions given the current market, he said.
Gold explorers and new producers would be in trouble with the value of the Australian dollar, he said.
"It's really the Aussie dollar which has killed it. The gold price is reasonably good if the Aussie dollar got back to 79 cents-78 (US) cents," he said.
"But at 81.29 cents it's pretty poor," he said.
Technical indicators suggested the price would look for further consolidation, with resistance at US$379.00/$380.00 an ounce and support at $376.00, he said.
Current trading at $376.00 left the market without much selling pressure at present, he said.
"When we go into the London time-zone you may see some more (selling)," he said.
Another Sydney dealer said Australian hedging was not occurring because the Australian dollar had pushed gold prices too low.
"We're not seeing any producers panicking or anything," he said.
Australian sales this morning was mainly dealers "just punting around", he said.
"In a technically weak market they're just looking for a quick turn in it," he said.
This dealer believed the market was likely to stay around the $375.00 strike level until after option expiry on Wednesday.
It was likely the market would stay between $374.00 and $378.00 until Wednesday, he said.
After Wednesday it was likely the market would go lower, with $373.00 the first target, then $370.00, he said.
"I don't necessarily see it stopping there. I can't see why it can't go to $360.00 myself," he said.
"Fundamentally I don't see anything particularly sound about it and we're just seeing people chasing it down more and more," he said.
"I think we can see it quite substantially down," he said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
